text:
acme-appops: heads up — after cert rotation this morning we're seeing intermittent TLS failures from some of our internal services to redwood private endpoints. errors in our app logs: "tls: handshake failure" and curl returns 52.

emma: sorry you're hitting this — is it all endpoints or a subset? any error samples you can paste?

acme-appops: only services that go through our HAProxy fronting cluster to the VPC endpoint. direct calls from dev boxes to the same ip:port succeed. sample curl from one failing pod:

```
curl -v https://private.redwood.example.com/api/health
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, handshake failure (552):
* SSL: no alternative certificates left
curl: (52) Empty reply from server
```

olivia: can you run `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private.redwood.example.com -showcerts` from a failing pod and a working host and paste outputs? also which cert rotation tool did you run?

acme-appops: we ran our k8s job that pulls new PEMs from vault and updates `/etc/ssl/redwood.pem` then runs `systemctl reload haproxy`. rotation logs show success. attaching failing pod openssl dump: 

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private.redwood.example.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN = private.redwood.example.com
   i:CN = Acme Intermediate CA
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
... (leaf) ...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

and from a working host the same command returns the full chain (leaf + intermediate + root) and verify OK.

cert-rotator-bot: rotation event: job/rotate-certs-2026-03-22 succeeded at 1761203400; updated secret redwood-cert-secret on nodes: node-1,node-2,node-3.

raj: interesting — rotator says it updated nodes 1..3, but your HAProxy cluster also has node-4 and node-5 that show failing in your earlier logs. can you confirm which haproxy instances are in the kubernetes daemonset vs. standalone?

acme-appops: right — node-4/5 are standalone appliances (managed by infra team) and we didn't include them in the k8s job. we thought they were pulling certs from the shared NFS mount but looks like they still have the old files.

emma: that could explain partial success. but your openssl on failing pod showed only leaf cert being presented — that suggests HAProxy on those appliances is loading the new PEM but missing intermediate in the file, or it's still serving the old file. can you `ls -l /etc/ssl/redwood.pem` and `openssl x509 -in /etc/ssl/redwood.pem -noout -text` on the appliance?

acme-appops: on node-4 `ls -l` shows timestamp updated, but `openssl x509 -in /etc/ssl/redwood.pem -noout -text` only prints leaf. we then checked `haproxy -c -f /etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg` and it returned OK, but `systemctl reload haproxy` exits 0 without applying — no errors.

olivia: sometimes HAProxy can keep an fd open to the old cert until a full restart or graceful reload that actually replaces the process. can you check `ss -plant | grep haproxy` and `ps aux | grep haproxy` to see if old pids remain? also check if there's a wrapper script that does `haproxy -f` vs systemd reload.

acme-appops: `ss` shows haproxy PID 1234 with open fd to /etc/ssl/redwood.pem. we tried `systemctl reload haproxy` again; journal shows reload invoked but child process failed to spawn because of a concurrent update to `/etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg` by a config management run. journal snippet:

```
Mar 22 09:12:01 node-4 systemd[1]: Reloading HAProxy service...
Mar 22 09:12:01 node-4 haproxy[1200]: Configuration file changed by concurrent process
Mar 22 09:12:01 node-4 systemd[1]: haproxy.service: Control process exited, code=exited status=1
```

raj: aha — so the cert file was updated but haproxy reload failed silently, leaving old process with old chain. that would make some clients (which hit node-4/5) fail. two paths: run a manual `systemctl restart haproxy` on the appliances (will cause brief connection disruption) or fix the rotation job to coordinate with config management and ensure a retry/backoff if reload fails.

emma: for an immediate mitigation, can you `systemctl restart haproxy` on node-4/5 and then re-run the `openssl s_client` check? also confirm the PEM on disk contains both the leaf and intermediate (order: leaf first, then intermediate). example bundle order we expect:

```
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
(leaf)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
(intermediate)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

acme-appops: restarted node-4, run openssl s_client -> verify OK, chain shows leaf+intermediate. curl from failing pod now returns 200. doing node-5 now.

deploy-bot: incident-note: temporary mitigation performed (manual restart) — impacted traffic window ~09:10-09:28 UTC.

olivia: nice. long-term we should update the rotation job to: 1) push certs to all haproxy instances (including appliances), 2) validate PEM contains full chain before reload, 3) attempt reload up to 3 times with exponential backoff, and 4) on persistent reload failure, fall back to restart or alert paging.

raj: i'll open a support ticket with the ops playbook and a recommended patch for your k8s job. also recommend adding a quick `openssl verify -CAfile /etc/ssl/ca-bundle.pem /etc/ssl/redwood.pem` step post-deploy so we catch missing intermediates.

acme-appops: thanks all — appreciate the quick help. can you also add a note about the concurrent config management race? our infra team will adjust timing. :thumbsup:

emma: yep we'll add that to the action items. leaving this thread open until we've pushed the rotation job fix.

acme-appops: ack — will follow up once infra schedules the config mgmt window change.

olivia: assigning follow-ups: [SUPPORT-1142] update rotation job (olivia/raj), [OPS-980] infra config window (acme infra). we'll close this once ticket shows merged change. :white_check_mark:
